custodianDisclosure: No. I administered none of the reviewed controls: no Azure resource, RBAC assignment, immutability policy, federated credential, GitHub ruleset, environment, tag, or pin record. My actions were read-only: reading the dossier, `git show`, `git ls-remote`, and `sha256sum` of the pinned workflow bytes. I made one mistake: a mistyped Windows path in a bash command created two scratch files and a directory (`tmp_u1*`) in the worktree root. I removed them, and no commit was made. I did not mutate any provider state.
selfReviewStatement: To the extent this session shows, I had no hand in the reviewed work. I was not the FK-P18-prime builder, the contract-drafting coordinator, the Azure/GitHub provisioning or pin-procedure actor, or a package-matrix repair subagent. I first encountered the dossier, `U1-verifier-pin.json`, and the pinned `u1-verify.yml` and `u1-produce.yml` in this review. I cannot rule out that the implementing sessions ran on the same model family. I have no knowledge of their identity or outputs, and that is not a role relationship.
rationale: FINDINGS, not ACCEPT. The prose is largely sound on the ratified selections. The pin is real: `git show be3e3de3:.github/workflows/u1-verify.yml` hashes to sha256:b7952e1e52f0144e7632fc73d8d04e9564184dfcf4c5af978c71592514cc4bbe, which matches `U1-verifier-pin.json`, and `git ls-remote` shows `refs/tags/u1-verifier-pin` -> be3e3de3dfcf6159d4ffb265aa39847aac5f0814. The two Entra identities, the environment-scoped federated credentials, `permissions: {}` at workflow top level, and the `candidate-sandbox` job (no environment, no login, no secrets) match the contract's shape. Under the contract's own rule 'do not accept on prose alone if a mechanism is missing', the material fails in four ways. (1) The pinned verifier is defective as written. It has no job-level `outputs:` anywhere, and its retention read-back compares a plain byte digest against a domain-wrapped digest, so it cannot produce a correct ACCEPT. (2) Several ratified or contract requirements are not enforced by any mechanism. Event-driven runs execute the head of `main`, not the pinned SHA. The lock state and the §5 INCOMPLETE fields are never checked, so the verifier can ACCEPT while the immutability policy is unlocked. Not-exercised rows and controls pass. The oracle is producer-authored. (3) The storage layer does not enforce the 'decision authored by the verifier identity' and 'producer submits only' claims. (4) Builder/custodian separation is not evidenced. Known open items: INCOMPLETE-U1-15..19 live rechecks are honestly bounded as dispatch-time acts, but nothing in the verifier or the contract makes an unrecorded recheck block ACCEPT or dispatch (F-4, F-15). Judged on those terms, U1-15..19 are named gaps, but the enforcement behind them is a hidden gap. The deferred lock flip is honestly disclosed but not honestly bounded. It lives only in an observation record (Part C) and the retention-plan literal, not in a contract amendment. The contract's ACCEPT precondition (§7.8: locked immutability observed) and the workflow's behaviour disagree, and the first-cycle outcome is undefined (F-4). The §8.5 evidence review being deferred is acceptable on its own, but no negative control NC-U1-01..13 has any executed evidence against these workflows, and the workflows themselves look unexecuted. Findings F-1 through F-5 must close before FK-P18-prime dispatch. Because the pin is already cut, closing F-1, F-2, F-3 and F-5 is a re-pin and therefore a contract amendment under standing #34.

findings.location: .github/workflows/u1-verify.yml @ be3e3de3 (sha256 b7952e1e...), all jobs; consumers at lines 164-165, 318, 329-332, 662, 684, 732-734, 845-847; U1-verifier-pin.json
findings.issue: The file declares no job-level `outputs:` mapping (grep for `outputs:` at job level returns nothing). In GitHub Actions, `steps.*.outputs` are not visible through `needs.<job>.outputs` unless the job maps them. Every `needs.resolve-request.outputs.*`, `needs.claim-attempt.outputs.*`, `needs.verify.outputs.*` and `needs.retention-observation.outputs.*` therefore evaluates to an empty string at run time. Consequences: the ledger PREFIX is `.../attempt-ledger/` with an empty request id; `SUBJECT_AND_SELECTION_DIGEST` is empty; `int(os.environ['ATTEMPT_NUMBER'])` at line 401 raises; close-attempt falls to 'interrupted'. The pinned verifier cannot reach a correct decision. The pin procedure froze these bytes. Basis: static analysis only. I did not execute the workflow, and actionlint is not installed.
findings.requiredChange: Add `outputs:` maps to resolve-request, claim-attempt, verify and retention-observation. Run actionlint and one full dry-run against the unlocked container, with its result recorded. Re-cut the pin (new workflowCommit, workflowFileSha256, tag move) as a recorded amendment, and re-submit for review. Do not dispatch FK-P18-prime on be3e3de3.

findings.location: u1-verify.yml verify step line 638 (decision_digest = doc_digest('foreman-line.u1.decision', decision)) vs retention-observation step lines 771-776 (readback = tag(raw); compare to recorded); contract IA-2.3, IA-4, §7.1
findings.issue: The recorded decision digest is the IA-2.3 domain-wrapped digest, sha256(canon({domain, apiVersion, payload})). The read-back digest is the plain SHA-256 of the stored bytes (`tag(raw)`). These can never be equal, so every run records result='mismatch', outcome='invalid' and exits 1. Even after F-1, the independent decision read-back can never succeed. The contract does not say which digest the read-back compares: byte digest or wrapper digest. IA-2 says only that 'artifact byte digests do not use the wrapper'.
findings.requiredChange: Amend IA-2/IA-4 to state that retention read-back compares exact stored bytes against the byte digest, and that IA-2.3 remains the detached document digest. Make the workflow compute both from the read-back bytes: parse, canonicalise, wrapper-digest, and compare to the recorded wrapper digest. Add a test that fails when the two are conflated.

findings.location: contract §3.1.1 / §2 item 3 vs u1-verify.yml lines 16-19 (workflow_run trigger), 288-311 and 703-722 (pin check), 292 and 707 (pin record read from raw.githubusercontent.com/.../main/...)
findings.issue: The event-driven path runs the default-branch copy of the workflow, not the pinned SHA. The pin check there is byte equality computed by the running file itself. A modified workflow simply omits the check. The only real control is the `main` ruleset, which requires a PR with required_approving_review_count=0 and has code-owner review off and a sole bypass actor (Part C). This violates the ratified clause 'executes from an independently protected workflow revision pinned by full commit SHA'. The pin record is also read from mutable `main`, so the verifier trusts a record in the same write domain as the file it checks. Disclosure is honest (note field of the pin record), but disclosure is not conformance.
findings.requiredChange: Either (a) remove `workflow_run` so only dispatch from `refs/tags/u1-verifier-pin` can produce an authoritative decision, or (b) add an amendment under which event-driven runs are labelled non-authoritative and cannot yield ACCEPT for FK-P19. For the dispatch path, read the pin record at the pinned commit or via the API by SHA, not from `main`. Perform the pin and PIN_DRIFT check before claim-attempt and resolve-request rather than only inside `verify` and `retention-observation`, so a drifted run cannot consume attempts.

findings.location: contract §5 header, §7.7, §7.8, INCOMPLETE-U1-11, INCOMPLETE-U1-15..19; u1-verify.yml lines 575-585 (configuration check), 787 (retentionStateObserved literal); U1-observations Part C 'Lock flip' ruling
findings.issue: The refusal 'every unrecorded §5 field raises U1_CONFIGURATION_INCOMPLETE and blocks ACCEPT' is prose only. The verifier checks only that the producer-authored retention-plan JSON has six keys and that the producer-authored `intervalDays` >= 400. No code path queries the container's immutability policy state, interval or etag. No code path checks U1-15..19. IA-7.7 is raised only for a missing key. The retention-observation 'observed state' is a hard-coded string literal, 'time-based-immutability 400d (unlocked pending lock flip...)', not an observation. Consequently the verifier can emit ACCEPT while the policy is Unlocked, which contradicts §7.8 'locked immutability (>= 400 days) observed' and INCOMPLETE-U1-11 'mode locked'. The lock deferral is recorded only in Part C, not as a contract amendment, and the contract's §11 still says the §5 acts precede dispatch. The interaction with the 3-attempt/24h budget is undefined. ACCEPT requires lock, the lock requires a first real bundle, and each re-verification consumes an attempt.
findings.requiredChange: (1) Give the verifier a management-plane Reader on the container and have it record the observed policy state, interval, immutabilityPeriodSinceCreation and etag. Emit INCOMPLETE/U1_CONFIGURATION_INCOMPLETE unless state is Locked and interval >= 400d. (2) Add a verifier-held checklist of §5 fields (a digest-pinned configuration record) that must be present before ACCEPT is possible. (3) Amend the contract to adopt the owner ruling of 2026-09-30 explicitly. State that the first evidence cycle is a non-ACCEPT shakedown, how the lock flip is recorded (etag), and that the post-flip verification runs under a new promotion request or a documented budget rule. (4) Delete the literal 'observed' string and replace it with a real read.

findings.issue: 'Not-exercised' passes. A not-exercised or gap row hits `continue` (lines 536-538, 566-567) and the invariant or control is never failed. A required invariant whose rows are all gaps ends with verdict 'ACCEPT' (line 528 default, line 550). All 13 controls can be gap rows and still yield ACCEPT. The control oracle is the producer's own `expected` compared to its own `observedResult`, and the comparison is skipped if either field is missing (line 572). Only the presence of `exitStatus` is checked (line 568), never its value. That is exactly the 'merely checks a producer-authored pass' construction §3.4.1 calls insufficient, and §3.4.2 forbids builder-supplied oracles. The contract text enables this: §7.6 allows 'an explicit not-exercised gap record (never a pass)' without limiting which controls may be gaps, and §3.4.1's 'source-authored' is ambiguous because the source is the builder's write surface. The derivation check (lines 540-545) validates only that producer classification matches producer signals. It never checks that the expected refusal was observed.
findings.requiredChange: (1) Amend §7.6/§3.4.4: only the three named PIN-09 inherited gaps may be gap rows, and any other gap or not-exercised row makes the invariant/control INCOMPLETE/U1_REQUIRED_EVIDENCE_MISSING. (2) Define the expected-outcome oracle as a coordinator-owned, digest-pinned record (referenced from the promotion request or trust policy), and make the verifier compare retained results against it. A missing `expected`/`observedResult` is a failure. (3) Make per-invariant ACCEPT require at least one exercised row whose signals show the expected refusal class (IA-5/IA-6 mapping). (4) Check exitStatus values, not just presence. (5) Implement or explicitly declare unsupported NC-U1-08.

findings.location: contract IA-5 (final paragraph), IA-6 (OQ-U1-08 ruling), §7.5; u1-verify.yml lines 503-526
findings.issue: Vacuous ACCEPT. `requiredInvariantIds` is 'a subset of IA-5 recorded by reviewed coordinator authority' and promotedRefusalClassIds is an owner parameter. An empty set is a subset, and §7.5 ('every ID in requiredInvariantIds has a result') is vacuously true. The verifier only compares the request to the bundle (lines 503-506). No minimum set exists, no check that a promoted refusal class is covered by a required invariant (IA-5 column 5), and OQ-U1-03 relaxes INV-U1-06 without stating what is required. A request with requiredInvariantIds=[] and promotedRefusalClassIds=[] yields ACCEPT with zero invariant evaluation.
findings.requiredChange: Amend IA-5: for the first promotion, ACCEPT requires at least INV-U1-01..05 (state the minimum) and every promoted refusal class must map to a required invariant. Make the verifier reject (INCOMPLETE/U1_REQUIRED_EVIDENCE_MISSING) any request whose set is smaller than the minimum or which promotes an uncovered class.

findings.location: contract IA-2.2, §3.2.3, §7.4 (promotion request undefined in IA-4); u1-verify.yml lines 99-107 and 128-131 (resolver), 312-319 (verify re-fetch), 498-502, 625
findings.issue: The 'immutable coordinator promotion request' has no closed schema in the contract: only a digest domain (IA-2.2) is named. Fields such as expectedSubjectDigest, selectedExecution, trustPolicyDigest, requiredInvariantIds exist only in workflow code. In the workflow: (a) the subject-equality check runs only `if expected_subject` (line 501), so a request without it skips §7.4/§3.2.3 silently; (b) trustPolicyDigest is copied to the decision (line 625) but never compared to anything, and policyDigest/compiledScopeDigest are never checked against reviewed authority; (c) the request is fetched from the mutable `main` head by the contents API; (d) the verify job re-fetches it (lines 312-319) without recomputing and comparing the resolver's digest, so a change on `main` between jobs is accepted (the comment 'digest-bound by the resolver' is untrue); (e) the event-driven path has no recorded digest to compare against; (f) several matching requests silently resolve to the last match (no break).
findings.requiredChange: Add a closed PromotionRequest shape to IA-4 with mandatory fields (expectedSubjectDigest, trustPolicyDigest, selectedExecution, invariant and refusal-class sets, oracle digest). Require all of them: a missing field is INCOMPLETE, never skipped. Fetch by commit SHA or blob SHA recorded in the dispatch input. Recompute and compare the digest in every job that consumes it, or pass one artifact. Reject zero or multiple matches.

findings.location: contract §3.3.2, §3.3.3, §3.1.3, IA-8, IA-9; U1-observations Part C (RBAC and 'Verifier decision-write role'); u1-verify.yml header lines 4-12, claim-attempt 143-267, close-attempt 826-886; u1-produce.yml environment u1-producer
findings.issue: Separation of powers is asserted in comments, not enforced at the storage layer. Both Entra roles are container-scope with no ABAC prefix conditions in the record; the workflow header claims prefix-limited writes ('ONLY the attempt-ledger prefix', 'decision/observation prefixes ONLY'). Azure RBAC at container scope cannot enforce that by itself. Consequences: (1) the producer identity, usable by any workflow on a protected branch via `environment: u1-producer` (OIDC subject binds to environment, not workflow file/ref), can create `runs/<id>/aNN/audit/decision.json` first. The verifier's `--overwrite false` then fails, or a consumer reads a producer-authored 'decision'. Nothing in the blob records its writer, and no Storage diagnostic log with requester object ID is observed. (2) The same producer identity writes the attempt ledger from the verifier workflow, so a builder-controlled workflow can forge or pre-create `aNN-dispatch/final` rows or STOP-REPORT and exhaust or fake the budget (§3.6.3). (3) The contract never says where the ledger lives, who writes it, or whether it is immutable: IA-8 says 'durable history' only. (4) The claim that the verifier role 'creates but never overwrites' rests on documentation review. The record shows no positive create test, no overwrite-denied probe, no producer-delete-denied probe, no role-definition JSON, and no assignment list. (5) `blobs/add/action` semantics for creating block blobs with `blobs/write` excluded are asserted from reference docs, not observed.
findings.requiredChange: Amend §3.3 and IA-8/IA-9 to require, as observed configuration: separate containers (or ABAC `startsWith` conditions) for evidence, ledger and decisions; a ledger writer identity separate from the builder-reachable producer workflow; federated credential subjects bound to the pinned workflow (custom OIDC claim template with job_workflow_ref and repository_id); and Storage diagnostic logging with requester identity retained outside the container. Attach the role definition JSON, `az role assignment list` at container, account, RG and subscription scope, and recorded denied-operation probes: producer delete, producer write under audit/, verifier overwrite, verifier out-of-prefix write.

findings.location: contract IA-9 (attemptPos), IA-4 'audit/decision.json under the same run qualifier', IA-8.5; u1-verify.yml lines 403-405 (producer prefix a{sel.attempt}), 447-448, 481-488, 666, 759-760; u1-produce.yml lines 410-411
findings.issue: `attemptPos` is ambiguous. In the producer it is GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT (a01). In the verifier it is the ledger attempt number K, and decision, verifier-context, retrieval-check and retention-observation are written into that same `runs/<producerRunId>/aKK/` prefix. The next verification attempt lists `producer_prefix` (the producer's `aNN`), sees `audit/decision.json` and `evidence/verifier-context/...` written by the prior attempt, finds them unlisted in `bundle.json` (lines 481-488), and fails INVALID/U1_ARTIFACT_INVALID. The first retry therefore poisons itself. The contract text (IA-4/IA-9) mandates co-location of decision and producer artifacts but defines no read rule that excludes audit and verifier objects.
findings.requiredChange: Amend IA-9 to use disjoint prefixes, e.g. `.../runs/<runId>/p<producerAttempt>/...` for producer objects and `.../verifications/<promotionRequestId>/a<K>/...` for verifier objects. State that the producer-package inventory excludes the verifier namespace and that audit objects are never part of the producer package.

findings.location: contract IA-4 (OQ-U1-07 paragraph), §3.5.3, §7.8; u1-verify.yml lines 658-673 (decision persisted), 729-809 (retention-observation), 789-797
findings.issue: Internal contradiction in the OQ-U1-07 ruling. The retention observation must carry 'an inventory entry in the bundle's evidence identity' and never be 'detached', yet it is written after the decision digest exists and is 'never referenced back into the already-hashed decision', while the producer's `bundle.json` inventory is already closed by the producer. The workflow writes it as an unlisted object (and that object triggers the F-9 'unlisted file' failure). No document lists it. Also, the ACCEPT decision blob is persisted before the read-back that is supposed to precede ACCEPT (§3.5.3/§7.1 say read-back precedes ACCEPT; the workflow persists `audit/decision.json` first and observes afterwards). A consumer reading only `audit/decision.json` sees ACCEPT even if the observation says mismatch, and the contract defines no consumer gate artifact.
findings.requiredChange: Define a verifier-authored seal document written last (e.g. `verifications/<id>/aKK/seal.json`) listing decision digest, retention-observation digest and result, and state that FK-P19 consumes only the seal. Alternatively, make the decision write conditional on a prior successful read-back of the producer package and the decision-candidate bytes. Rewrite the OQ-U1-07 paragraph so it is non-contradictory.

findings.location: contract §3.1.2, §3.4.1, §3.4.5, IA-7.4, IA-7.9, NC-U1-05/06/09; u1-produce.yml lines 185-216 (feed), 229-238 (producer-identity), 275-290 (independence-model); u1-verify.yml lines 42-71, 326-657
findings.issue: The 'independent' evidence is committed static FK-P17 JSON that the producer packages (EVIDENCE_DIR defaults to the repo's `bypass-outage-harness/evidence`). No CI job generates or re-executes it. `producer-identity` nonetheless labels the CI run `evidenceOrigin`, implying the run produced the evidence. The candidate-sandbox output is uploaded but never downloaded or consumed by the verifier (no `download-artifact`), and the sandbox is off by default, so §3.4.5 'derive independently' degenerates to re-reading producer rows. The verifier never queries the GitHub run API to confirm that runId/workflow/head_sha/event/conclusion exist and match, so IA-7.4 (U1_PROVENANCE_INVALID) and IA-7.9 (U1_INDEPENDENCE_UNPROVEN) are unreachable. The object name `runs/<runId>/...` is the only link between a blob and a run. The contract has no requirement that controls be executed within a recorded run, so a literal reading admits laptop-generated JSON (see naive reading N7). A candidate-controlled sandbox can also pre-create artifacts named `u1-verifier-decision` / `u1-verifier-observation` in the shared run artifact namespace, which makes the later `upload-artifact` fail. Opt-in only.
findings.requiredChange: Amend §3.4.1/§3.1.2 to require that every negative control and observation row record the identity (run, job, commit) of the execution that produced it. Have the verifier confirm those identities through the GitHub API, raise IA-7.4/7.9 on mismatch or absence, and consume the sandbox output as untrusted data for the independent derivation (or state the controls as unsupported until it does). Correct `evidenceOrigin` to name the true origin. Use a random/unique artifact name for sandbox output.

findings.location: contract §3.1.4, §3.2.1, §5 INCOMPLETE-U1-14; U1-observations Part C 'GitHub protection evidence' (rulesets 24257508, 22369510, 24258920; environments u1-verifier / u1-producer; CODEOWNERS), 'pin procedure COMPLETE' (75d718b)
findings.issue: A control custodian 'distinct from the FK-P18-prime builder' is not evidenced. m0r6aN is simultaneously owner, custodian, sole bypass actor on all three branch/tag rulesets, sole required reviewer of `u1-verifier` with prevent_self_review=false, the approver of PRs (count=0), and the person at whose authority the coordinator session ran `gh`/`az`. The pin record (75d718b) was pushed directly to `main` using that bypass. `required_approving_review_count=0`, `require_code_owner_review=false`, so CODEOWNERS is an annotation (Part C says so). A bypass actor was also added to `main-pr-gate` to get past a red baseline, with no sunset. The observation record says the approval gate will be restored 'when a second write-access identity exists (e.g., the FK-P18-prime builder identity)', but that is not a dispatch precondition anywhere. If the builder session runs with the owner's token, every protection is void. §9.2 assumes operator honesty. It does not address a builder that shares the operator's credentials.
findings.requiredChange: Record the builder identity and token scope in §5 (INCOMPLETE-U1-14). Make a precondition of dispatch that the builder credential has no bypass, admin, environment-approval or tag-ruleset rights. Make restoring required_approving_review_count>=1 plus require_code_owner_review a dispatch precondition as soon as the builder identity exists. Record a sunset/revert criterion for the `main-pr-gate` bypass.

findings.location: contract §3.1.5, §3.3.4, INCOMPLETE-U1-17; u1-produce.yml lines 247-256; u1-verify.yml verifier-context (595-606)
findings.issue: Runner identity. The contract says 'a mutable runner label is not a tested identity (INF-4)' (§3.1.5, §3.3.4) but the selected runner is exactly a mutable label, `ubuntu-24.04`. No contract text carves out the exception; the 'limitation recorded' exists only in the producer-generated `toolchain.json` at run time and is not a reviewable contract clause. The recorded reason, 'hosted-runner image digest is not exposed to jobs', understates what is available: the hosted image's `ImageOS`/`ImageVersion` environment variables and RUNNER_* values are exposed and could be recorded. The verifier's `verifier-context` records no runner identity at all, although the verifier is the party whose isolation matters.
findings.requiredChange: Amend §3.3.4 with an explicit, reasoned exception: GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04` is accepted at label level with image version recorded, and this limitation is part of the §9 assumed boundaries. Record ImageOS, ImageVersion, RUNNER_NAME/OS/ARCH and the az CLI version in producer and verifier jobs. Define the closure criterion for INCOMPLETE-U1-17.

findings.location: contract §3.1.6, OQ-U1-04, INCOMPLETE-U1-18; u1-produce.yml lines 41-48 and 392-394 (permissions); u1-verify.yml (no attest step)
findings.issue: Attestation posture is coherent (corroborator-only, never consumed) but unreachable: neither workflow requests `attestations: write` or runs an attest step, so INCOMPLETE-U1-18 ('issuance capability exercised for the selected event') cannot be satisfied by the pinned verifier. The producer workflow is not under the pin, but any addition to it is a builder change. The contract does not say what U1-18 yields when no attestation is issued.
findings.requiredChange: Amend §5/§3.1.6: INCOMPLETE-U1-18 is recorded as 'not issued by the selected workflows' (a named gap that never affects status), or add the issuance step through a recorded amendment. State explicitly that absence of an attestation never changes the decision status.

findings.location: contract §3.5.5, INCOMPLETE-U1-19, §9.2; U1-observations Part C federated credentials u1-verifier-fc / u1-producer-fc; U1-verifier-pin.json
findings.issue: Trust-root and revocation. Honestly named as a dispatch-time act, but no consequence and no minimum content are specified. (1) Nothing in the verifier or contract blocks dispatch or ACCEPT when U1-19 is unrecorded (see F-4). (2) There is no revocation semantics for accepted decisions: the store is append-only and §3.5.5 covers only loss. A compromise found after an ACCEPT has no representable revocation record that FK-P19 must consult. (3) The federated subjects are `repo:m0r6aN/agent-skills:environment:...`, i.e. bound to a repository name, not the immutable repository ID, so rename/transfer/delete-and-recreate takes over the trust root. (4) The trust root is stated as the repo itself, which is in the builder's write domain. (5) The procedure for rotating the pin, FICs and role assignments after compromise is not given.
findings.requiredChange: Write a minimum revocation procedure into the contract now: delete or disable the federated credentials and role assignments, re-pin by amendment, append a verifier-authored revocation record under a defined prefix that FK-P19 must check, and state what happens to decisions issued during the compromise window. Bind the federated subjects to repository_id and job_workflow_ref. Make 'U1-19 unrecorded' an enforced IA-7.7 condition.

findings.issue: Size and count limits are applied after every object has been downloaded (lines 452-467). Blob list metadata (contentLength) is not used to reject early. `json.loads` and the depth function run unguarded (a deeply nested document raises RecursionError before the depth-16 check) or outside any typed handler (line 557 has none), so hostile input crashes the step instead of yielding INVALID/U1_EVIDENCE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, and burns an attempt. Python's `json.loads` accepts NaN/Infinity and duplicate keys while IA-2 admits neither.
findings.requiredChange: Check count and total size from the list metadata before any download. Parse with a depth-limited, duplicate-key-rejecting, NaN-rejecting parser, and map every parse failure to INVALID/U1_ARTIFACT_INVALID.

findings.location: u1-verify.yml lines 270, 318, 674, 821, 889 (backticks inside double-quoted echo; expression interpolation into shell), 91-97, 171, 405, 879 (request id in API paths/blob names); u1-produce.yml line 385
findings.issue: `${{ needs.resolve-request.outputs.promotion-request-id }}` (from file content, unvalidated) is interpolated directly into a shell command at line 318. Unquoted backticks inside double-quoted `echo` strings (270, 674, 821, 889; also u1-produce.yml 385) are command substitution; the summary text is lost and arbitrary content could execute. The request id is also used unsanitised in blob names and API paths.
findings.requiredChange: Validate promotionRequestId against a closed grammar (e.g. [a-z0-9-]{1,64}) in the resolver. Pass values via `env:` instead of expression interpolation. Use escaped or single-quoted backticks.

findings.location: contract IA-8 (digest under IA-2.5), §3.3.3 and INCOMPLETE-U1-04/-09/-10; u1-verify.yml lines 256-265, 594; U1-observations Part C storage account, RBAC, network rows
findings.issue: (a) Ledger rows are hashed with a bare byte digest (line 265), not under IA-2.5 as IA-8 requires. (b) `retrieval-check.digestMismatches` emits note indexes (line 594) rather than object names or digests. (c) The storage account `bs2jhgwvduljfdwdp` sits in the shared `biostack-rg`. No record shows which other principals hold write/Authorization/Owner at account, RG or subscription scope (they could change the policy while it is Unlocked, or re-enable shared-key access). The account `defaultAction: Allow` network posture is recorded but undecided, and INCOMPLETE-U1-09/10 remain partial. The custodian holds Data Contributor at account scope, which covers every container in the shared account.
findings.requiredChange: Digest ledger rows under IA-2.5 and put real object digests in retrieval-check. Record all principals with write, delete or authorization rights at account, RG and subscription scope. Record a decision on the network posture. naiveReadingTests: Each reading below is constructed to be wrong but literal, and tested against the contract prose. N1: ACCEPT with all 13 controls as 'not-exercised' gap rows. N11: 'a producer-authored status is never the decision' (§3.1.3) read as covering only status, verdict, check summary, runner label, and attestation predicate. methodNotes: Method: full read of Parts 0, A, B, C and D of the dossier, with the lines elided in the display (894, 920) read in full. I then read the actual pinned workflows from git (`be3e3de3:.github/workflows/u1-verify.yml` and `u1-produce.yml`, which the dossier does not include) in full. I hash-checked the verify file against the pin record (match), confirmed via `git ls-remote` that the tag points to be3e3de3, and read the pin record on origin/main (fields match). I confirmed `.github/CODEOWNERS` covers the listed paths and that no `promotion-requests/` directory exists on origin/main. Findings come from static analysis of the workflows against the contract clauses; hostile-input probing was done by reasoning about inputs (empty sets, absent fields, gap rows, name collisions), not by running them. Limitations: (1) I did not execute either workflow, run actionlint (not installed), or make any call to GitHub or Azure, so every live-state claim (rulesets, environments, role assignments, immutability state, federated credentials) is taken from the dossier's Part C record and is unobserved by me. (2) F-1 and F-2 rest on GitHub Actions semantics (job `outputs:` must be declared) and on reading the digest functions; I am confident but did not run them.
